title: Brandon Weems promoted to general manager by Cleveland Cavaliers on September 18, 2026
dek: Brandon Weems, who joined the Cleveland Cavaliers organization as a scout in 2015, was promoted to general manager on September 18, 2026. Weems ascends to the role after holding posts as director of scouting, director of player personnel, and assistant general manager since 2022, succeeding Mike Gansey, who left to become president of basketball operations for the Philadelphia 76ers.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Weems spent over a decade with a single franchise, advancing internally through four distinct front-office roles, a stability play in an era of frequent executive turnover.
bottom_line: Weems's mandate as GM unfolds in the context of Gansey's move to Philadelphia and James's choice to join the 76ers, not Cleveland. The immediate test is how Weems shapes the Cavaliers' roster in the season ahead and whether the continuity of internal promotion translates to competitive performance on the court.
body:
The Cleveland Cavaliers promoted Brandon Weems to general manager on September 18, 2026, per Yahoo NBA reporting of an announcement made by ESPN's Shams Charania. Weems, who originally joined the Cavaliers organization as a scout in 2015, has held the roles of director of scouting, director of player personnel, and assistant general manager before his promotion to the top basketball operations role.
Weems became assistant general manager in 2022 and now operates under President of Basketball Operations Koby Altman. The promotion follows Mike Gansey's departure to the Philadelphia 76ers, where Gansey took the post of president of basketball operations this past offseason, creating a vacancy for the Cavaliers GM role.
Altman issued a statement on the promotion: "Brandon has earned this opportunity through more than a decade of exceptional work with the Cavaliers and by consistently demonstrating elite judgment and the expertise required to help lead our basketball operations."
The promotion received attention beyond the organization. LeBron James posted a congratulatory message on September 18, 2026: "YESSIR!!!! Congratulations my brother @BrandonWeems10 !! Proud of you man."
During the offseason, there was speculation that the Cavaliers would leverage Weems's pre-existing relationship with James to lure the player back to Cleveland. ESPN's Brian Windhorst noted at the time that this framing was a disservice to Weems's body of work and standing within the organization independent of any player recruitment.
